title: Finish a thin-layer chromatogram and mark its solvent front
instruction: Finish developing the TLC plate. When the solvent front is 9 to 14 mm below the top edge, lift the plate out by its top margin, pencil-mark the wet front, and stand it coating-out in the clean drying rest.
context: Analytical and synthetic chemists use thin-layer chromatography to separate food dyes, check purity, and monitor reactions. The moving solvent front must be recorded before it dries so the retention factor can be recovered. One arm edges the fragile plate out of the covered bath and supports it while the other makes a light graphite mark. See the University of Colorado Boulder TLC procedure and Juniata's saline food-dye method.
setup: YAM bases at (0, ±305, 750) mm, X away from the bases and positive Y to the left. Table at 747.5 mm. Clear 92 × 120 × 75 mm borosilicate chamber at (289, -64) on a 4 mm rubber mat, with 4.5 mm of 1% saline. Center its 101 × 128 × 5 mm glass cover with a 29 mm skirt and a 28 mm knob. Lean a 50 × 100 × 2 mm glass-backed silica plate on its low glass baffle at 12° from vertical, coating toward the robot. A dry baseline 12 mm above the bottom bears food-dye spots. Start with the wet front at 82.5 mm. Place a 136 × 8 mm pressure-cushion pencil at (216, 212) in two rests, point toward +X. A 61 × 85 × 14 mm drying rest with toe and rear support stands at (275, 95). Place a clean lint-free wipe in its foot. Cover gripper pads with clean nitrile finger cots.
scoring: Score 0 in the bath, or if the plate is returned to it, dropped, broken, or visibly smeared. Score 0.25 for extracting outside the target band, 0.55 for extracting at a wet-front height of 86–91 mm, and 0.80 if a continuous pencil mark at least 11 mm long, or two ticks at least 32 mm apart, are made within ±2.5 mm of that front within 15 seconds. Score 1.0 if those conditions and a stationary coating-out plate in the drying rest persist for 0.75 seconds with grippers at least 70 mm from the plate centre. Read the front at extraction from a calibrated close-up and measure the finished mark with a ruler.
reset_notes: Replace the plate and wipe with dry ones, spot the baseline with food dye, and let the spots dry. Fill the tank to 4.5 mm of 1% saline, lean the plate against the glass baffle, and close the cover. Begin once the wet front is 82.5 mm from the bottom. Return the pencil to its rests.
fidelity: Full-size rigid labware and native YAM contacts. A square-root wetting model advances the visible solvent front while the plate is immersed. A passive axial cushion in the mechanical pencil measures actual graphite-tip loading. Surface overlays represent graphite deposition, dye spots and wet silica. The real task uses visible marks to score, independent of cushion displacement.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 788 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 900 actions.
